content: 1. Cyclizine and hyoscyamine both reduce cholinergic effects and transmission. Use these drugs with caution and monitor the patient closely. 2. Cyclobenzaprine and hyoscyamine also decrease cholinergic effects and transmission. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 3. Methylene blue and cyclobenzaprine both elevate serotonin levels. This combination is serious and should be avoided or replaced with an alternative drug. Methylene blue increases serotonin due to its inhibition of monoamine oxidase A (MAO-A). If methylene blue must be administered, discontinue serotonergic drugs immediately and monitor for central nervous system (CNS) toxicity. Serotonergic therapy can be resumed 24 hours after the last dose of methylene blue or after two weeks of monitoring, whichever comes first. 4. Methylene blue and cyproheptadine are contraindicated. MAO inhibitors may prolong and intensify the anticholinergic effects of antihistamines. Cyproheptadine may reduce the serotonergic effects of MAO inhibitors. 5. Darifenacin and hyoscyamine both decrease cholinergic effects and transmission. Use caution and monitor closely. 6. Hyoscyamine increases the effects of daxibotulinumtoxinA through pharmacodynamic synergy. Use caution and monitor closely. Drugs with anticholinergic effects may enhance the effects of botulinum toxin, potentially causing excessive neuromuscular weakness and heightened systemic anticholinergic effects. 7. Methylene blue and deutetrabenazine both increase each other's toxicity through sympathetic (adrenergic) effects, including elevated blood pressure and heart rate. This combination is contraindicated. Deutetrabenazine should not be used with an MAOI or within 14 days of discontinuing MAOI therapy. If methylene blue must be used emergently, discontinue deutetrabenazine and monitor for adverse effects. Deutetrabenazine can be resumed 24 hours after the last dose of methylene blue or after two weeks of monitoring, whichever comes first. 11. MAOI interactions with opioids may manifest as serotonin syndrome or opioid toxicity (e.g., respiratory depression, coma). Opioids are not recommended for patients taking MAOIs or within 14 days of stopping MAOIs. If urgent opioid treatment is needed, use test doses and frequent titration of small doses to treat pain while closely monitoring blood pressure and signs of CNS and respiratory depression. 48.
